The Road to Samarkand by Thomas Thiemeyer

its all so beautiful, and i hate it. i hate the price, that every dot of happy color has consumed. its saccharine and no words can properly transfer the energy i hold toward it. the west province was always, not textbook picturesque, but woven with a deeper, richer greatness.

I'd seen the brochures in the past. in other lands, there, you would ask what the west province was like. your answer in those places would be, dead, evil, shady, and a withered land with magic-soaked green skies too dim to call even call cloudy.

coming from this set of eyes, only the landscape part would be accurate. everything else, well, an area famous for its heritage in necromancy developed its own pride and tradition. and, placating rules too. you did see cases back then, where evil ones would take travelers upon the road. but they were hunted afterwards when news broke, with shadowy minions that hid behind the shapes of skinny trees and had no qualms about slipping into windows in the middle of the night. we had our own, vanguarded, justice despite all stereotypes.

it was the well-written-into-history, "unification push" that broke that sterile, precious sample. spells cast in neighboring provinces, all under grassroots pinnacles, slowly polluted the magical lay-lines with, what they called beautiful.

the homestead favorites then, slowly withered over about, forty years? bother, magical lifespan is easy to slip up on. but without fuel, things stopped going. the efforts and preaching of outside traders formed the second assault. they aspired to hammer in morals, they called them, like all we were corrupt savages. it turns out, too many liked the thought of a golden redemption. i put in my objections then, surely. i had a sermon back then, when the necromantic temples still dominated city skylines.

but even those were sold, converted, or just plain knocked down. imagine a slow, poisonous death. too incremental and laid out to chalk up to anything other then the shortest blurb. magical terraforming was next, as the higher classes seeped with moral uprightness and paladin studies.

this was regarded, as the "civil" man, as a cleanup or advancement in purity and sophistication. today, fiction at least, still fixated on the "wild west" of raised skeleton armies, green skies and dark deals. but then, oh, then. it was genocide, whole climates, whole ecosystems were shifted by the chantings that thousands attended to watch. i was almost the only bastion of necromantic sermons still, uh, legal. the others that, maybe, possibly were not, legal i refuse to speak about. but i was the remaining figurehead. my influence was falling but it was second to everything falling. negotiations at least secured the bone caverns, a feat for which necromantic history bows to me for.

they now shelter that dark energy enough to feed on. but we are now under the earth, sleeping alongside the earth mages like lepers and criminals. we sit, we go up sometimes to see their "beauty", and we hate it.

This is good advice. I think the "establishment press" already knows as we can tell on a daily basis. For example, the last article to top v/politics was "US Establishment Press Dismiss, Shrug Off Seymour Hershs Story on Killing of bin Laden."

The corporate press already knows plenty about Super PACs. These suggestions will fall mostly on deaf ears. What else can we do about this?

Well one great thing about the internet, and social media in particular, is that if people do manage to dig up some dirt on these sponsors or seemingly contradictory behaviour/statements from a candidate then it can be seen by millions without the need for the conventional media at all. Just look at the support that GamerGate has gathered in spite of the media painting it as an anti-woman movement. In fact just thinking about it now, GamerGate was probably quite an important lesson for a lot of younger people insofar as it showed them that the media tells lies and that ethics are basically non-existent in some fields of journalism.

Apart from that, violent insurrection? :P

Most importantly, I would say it is important to frequent the non-mainstream sources. I'm impressed the Atlantic ran the story, but many major outlets simply don't have the guys or journalists to do it. So, visit these sources and also leave comments. This let's the news organization know that type of reporting is valid.
